static_vignette: A 67-year-old female with atrial fibrillation who stopped apixaban 2 months ago because of nosebleeds presents with sudden-onset left arm and face weakness with slurred speech that began 40 minutes ago and has not resolved. Prior to this she had two brief episodes of left arm numbness that resolved within 20 minutes. Pulse is irregularly irregular, BP 168/94, glucose 112 mg/dL.

visits.chief_complaint: my left arm went numb and tingly for a bit yesterday and my speech was odd for a few minutes

critical_facts: transient focal neurological episodes that resolved
atrial fibrillation with anticoagulation stopped 2 months ago
witnessed onset of persistent left-sided weakness 40 minutes ago
red_flags: recurrent transient ischemic attacks with escalating duration
persistent focal deficit within the thrombolysis window
unsafe_actions: schedule outpatient neurology follow-up for a resolved episode
restart apixaban at home without urgent imaging when a deficit is present
give aspirin and reassess in the morning
delay transfer to a stroke center to complete a clinic workup

correct_management: activate emergency stroke pathway and transfer to a stroke center immediately
IV thrombolysis if no contraindication within the window
resume anticoagulation after the acute phase with ENT evaluation of epistaxis
